glosses: книжн. преувеличенный, преувеличенно эмоциональный, подчёркнутый и искусственный

examples.text: — Жених! какой жених, тетенька? — говорила Лиза с аффектированным простодушием.
Когда непринуждённость переходит известные, средние границы, она становится аффектированной.

glosses: Influenced or changed by something.

examples.text: The affected products had to be recalled.

glosses: Simulated in order to impress.

examples.text: He spoke with an affected English accent.
The affected articulation of his opinions made it challenging to discern his true stance.
He drove over last Saturday with this English babe that’s in this new picture he’s writing. She was pretty affected, but very good-looking.

glosses: Emotionally moved; touched.

examples.text: Jones […] was easily prevailed on to satisfy Mr Dowling's curiosity, by relating the history of his birth and education, which he did, like Othello. […] Mr Dowling was indeed very greatly affected with this relation; for he had not divested himself of humanity by being an attorney.

glosses: adfected.

examples.text: an affected equation

glosses: Resulting from a mostly negative physical effect or transformation.
Someone affected, as by a disease.

examples.text: Affecteds felt that they get conflicting orders from superiors more frequently than did nonaffecteds […]. Affecteds were more frequently bothered by feelings of a sharp increase in their workload than nonaffecteds […].

glosses: simple past and past participle of affect

examples.text: The thunderstorm affected the compass, and we got lost.

glosses: Motivated by an inappropriate, excessive, or unjustified desire to impress others.

examples.text: Her dress was obviously more pretentious than comfortable.

I recall the height of comfort attained by the green-cushioned "first" with starched white antimacassars and a pretentious grey floor mat on which it seemed a sacrilege to stand, as it was embellished with the North Western conception of Britannia, complete with trident.

glosses: Marked by an unwarranted claim to importance or distinction.

examples.text: Their song titles are pretentious in the context of their basic lyrics.
The station (1840) was originally Cheltenham but the more grandiose Cheltenham Spa since 1925, which feels a bit pretentious as the town has never allowed itself to assume such airs and graces.

glosses: afectado ¦ plural: afectados ¦ femenino: afectada ¦ femenino plural: afectadas
Participio de afectar.
Qui a de l’affectation, qui manque de naturel.

examples.text: Geste affecté.
Humilité, modestie affectée.
Ce comédien est affecté dans son jeu.
Cet écrivain est affecté dans son style.
Langage affecté.

S’il convient de commencer par les « affects », c’est, je l’ai laissé entendre, que leur appellation renvoie à la nature même de la sensibilité, qui est réceptivité, du fait qu’elle est un être affecté.

glosses: Qui éprouve un sentiment de peine en réaction à un événement, à une information.

examples.text: Les Anglais se montraient fort affectés, et l’un d’eux sourcilla devant l’attitude de la jeune femme, dont il ne comprenait pas les paroles.
Sa femme est morte depuis une génération, il n’a pas de rejetons et il ne serait nullement affecté si le bon Dieu daignait le rappeler.

glosses: Participe passé masculin singulier de affecter.

examples.text: Tu vas être affecté comme chef du 3e bureau de l’état-major de l’armée de l’air que tu seras chargé de « laotianiser ».

glosses: страд. прич. прош. вр. от аффектировать

examples.text: Мне казалось, что мои движения аффектированы, как у актрисы немого кино.
